- Model consistently overestimates prices in early forecast periods, especially after sharp spikes; reduce initial forecast values by 1–3%.
- Model underestimates prices during prolonged downward trends; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- Forecast tends to lag true price movements by 1–3 days; adjust forward by 0.5–1.5% per day for lagged declines.
- After a price spike, model overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 2–5% immediately after a spike, then gradually revert.
- Model exhibits persistent bias toward higher values in mid-forecast horizon; apply downward correction of 1–3% for days 15–25.
- Forecast often fails to capture true volatility clustering; increase standard deviation adjustment by 10–20% during high-variance periods.
